issues.description: The template Main.java shows example constructor calls for Seal, Pig, and Goat using two parameters (e.g. new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), whereas the problem specification and the solution use single-argument constructors (only name). This discrepancy can confuse students about the required constructor signature for the animal classes.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Main.java example consistent with the specified UML and solution: update the commented example constructor calls to use single-argument constructors (e.g. new Seal("Clarabelle"), new Pig("Doodle"), new Goat("Buttinsky")). Alternatively, if two-argument constructors are intended, update the problem statement and solution to document and implement those constructors.

issues.description: The template Farm.java declares the private helper method without an Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)), while the UML in the problem statement and the solution implementation define singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This signature mismatch between template and solution/description may confuse students about the expected helper method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Uncomment or add the Animal parameter in the template Farm.java helper signature to match the UML and solution: change the declaration to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). Also update any template comments to reflect the intended signature so students implement the correct method.
